title: Discount Variant Quality Checklist and Economic Calibrator
content:
Summary:

This working doc defines a compact, operational checklist and a lightweight cost calibrator for evaluating lower-cost inference variants (quantized models, smaller families, reduced context lengths, lower-precision kernels). The goal is to tie automated quality gates to measured economic impact so product teams can safely adopt discounted variants where the tradeoff is acceptable.

Audience:
- Product managers owning per-route unit economics
- ML engineers running evals and rollouts
- Platform/ops who implement rollout automation and metrics

Why this doc exists (problem statement):
Teams want to reduce per-token cost using cheaper inference variants, but currently we lack a standardized way to:
1) quantify the expected cost delta for a candidate variant,
2) set defensible quality tolerances based on user-impact classes, and
3) automate a gate decision that is both conservative and cost-aware. This doc proposes a simple spreadsheet model plus an eval checklist to operationalize the gate.

Key definitions (for this doc):
- Discount variant: any model/configuration that reduces inferred unit cost vs baseline (e.g., int8 quant, smaller-llm, seq-truncation).
- Unit quality metric: route-specific primary metric (e.g., ROUGE-L for summarization, top-1 accuracy for classification, embedding cosine for search).
- Quality delta (ΔQ): baseline_metric - variant_metric (positive if variant is worse).
- Cost delta (ΔC): baseline_cost_per_1k_tokens - variant_cost_per_1k_tokens (positive if variant is cheaper).
- Cost tolerance threshold: minimum ΔC required to justify a given ΔQ for a route class.

Spreadsheet: DiscountVariantCostModel.xlsx (expected columns)
- Col A: variant_id (e.g., q8_7b_v2)
- Col B: baseline_model (e.g., gpt-neo-13b)
- Col C: route (e.g., user-summarize, background-embedding)
- Col D: baseline_unit_cost_per_1k (USD)
- Col E: variant_unit_cost_per_1k (USD)
- Col F: baseline_metric (float)
- Col G: variant_metric (float)
- Col H: ΔQ (formula: =F - G)
- Col I: ΔC (formula: =D - E)
- Col J: sample_size (N) used for metric calculation
- Col K: p_value_or_conf_int (optional)
- Col L: economic_score (formula below)

Economic score (single scalar used by gate):
We propose a normalized score that blends relative quality loss with dollars saved:
- RelativeQualityLoss = max(0, ΔQ / baseline_metric)
- RelativeCostSaving = max(0, ΔC / D)
- EconomicScore = RelativeCostSaving / (1 + α * RelativeQualityLoss)
Where α (alpha) is a tunable sensitivity parameter (suggest α = 5 for user-facing routes, α = 2 for background jobs). Store alpha in the spreadsheet per-route.

Acceptance logic (high level):
- For each candidate variant compute EconomicScore.
- Compare EconomicScore to route-specific gate thresholds (Threshold_user, Threshold_background).
- Require minimum sample size (see sampling below) and non-trivial statistical evidence (p < 0.10 for fast checks, p < 0.05 for production rollouts).

Suggested route classes and default gates (examples)
- User-facing interactive (chat, summarization, codegen): α = 5, Threshold = 0.08, max ΔQ tolerated = 1.5% absolute drop in primary metric.
- Async user-visible (email summary, nightly reports): α = 3, Threshold = 0.06, max ΔQ = 3% absolute.
- Background / batch (embeddings for search reindex, similarity for internal pipelines): α = 2, Threshold = 0.03, max ΔQ = 5% absolute.
These are starting points — routes with revenue or legal sensitivity should use much higher alpha and lower Threshold.

Sampling guidance
- Minimum N by route type (rule of thumb):
  - Interactive routes: N >= 2k samples
  - Async user-visible: N >= 5k samples
  - Background/analytics: N >= 1k samples
- Stratify by input length buckets and user locale if these factors materially affect metric variance.
- If variance is high, use bootstrap CI on ΔQ and require upper bound of CI to be within max ΔQ tolerance.

Cost estimation details (plug into columns D/E)
- Use model-specific throughput numbers from serving runtime (tokens/sec) and pricing per-GPU-hour to convert to USD per 1k tokens.
- Example micro-calculation (spreadsheet formula):
  - tokens_per_call_avg (column M)
  - calls_per_hour (col N)
  - tokens_per_hour = M * N
  - GPU_hours_needed = tokens_per_hour / (throughput_tokens_per_gpu_hour)
  - USD_hourly_gpu = from pricing table
  - unit_cost_per_1k = (GPU_hours_needed * USD_hourly_gpu) / (tokens_per_hour / 1000)
- In practice we precompute unit_cost_per_1k per variant for typical request shapes and store a small lookup table in the sheet. Keep single-token-weighted and full-sequence-weighted cost lines for sensitivity.

Example scenarios (concrete numbers)
- Baseline: baseline_unit_cost_per_1k = $0.12, baseline_metric = 0.78 (task accuracy), variant: variant_unit_cost_per_1k = $0.06, variant_metric = 0.755
  - ΔQ = 0.025 absolute (3.2% relative loss)
  - ΔC = 0.06 (50% saving)
  - RelativeQualityLoss = 0.025/0.78 = 0.032
  - RelativeCostSaving = 0.5
  - For α=5: EconomicScore = 0.5 / (1 + 5*0.032) ≈ 0.5 / (1 + 0.16) = 0.43
  - If threshold for interactive is 0.08, score 0.43 > 0.08 -> passes cost gate, but check absolute ΔQ = 2.5% > 1.5% max for interactive, so blocked by absolute cap.
Note: Always evaluate both the scalar gate and absolute ΔQ caps.

Quality gate automation recipe (rollout automation integration)
1) Pre-register candidate variant in spreadsheet and compute EconomicScore.
2) Kick off a mini-eval job (N based on route type) that outputs baseline_metric, variant_metric, CI and p-value. Store results in artifacts bucket and update the sheet row.
3) Automated gate checks: (a) sample size and p-value thresholds, (b) EconomicScore >= route_threshold, (c) ΔQ <= max_abs_loss. If all true, mark variant as "eligible-for-canary".
4) Canary rollout: 1% traffic for 24h with real traffic collection. Monitor rolling metrics and cost. If no regression beyond tolerated bounds, expand to 10% then 50% with automated stop conditions if metric drift observed.

Monitoring & post-rollout checks
- Required signals in the Console per-rollout: token-level cost, per-route metric (primary and secondary), error rate, tail latency, and fallback rate.
- Alert if rolling ΔQ exceeds 2x the evaluation ΔQ or if CostSavings falls below 60% of expected (indicating misestimated throughput).

Safeguards and conservative adjustments
- For routes with small user base or high variance, multiply α by 2 to be conservative.
- If the variant uses a new kernel or not-yet-verified quant library, require a dedicated safety buffer: reduce reported ΔC by 20% when computing RelativeCostSaving until validated in production.
- For enterprise customers with SLAs, require 0.01% false positive budget and human sign-off.

Checklist for running a candidate eval (copyable)
- [ ] Register variant_id and baseline in spreadsheet (cols A-F)
- [ ] Confirm tokens_per_call distribution in sheet (col M)
- [ ] Compute unit costs (cols D/E) using current pricing table
- [ ] Run stratified eval with N >= required sample size
- [ ] Record baseline_metric and variant_metric and compute ΔQ, ΔC (cols H/I)
- [ ] Compute EconomicScore (col L) using route α
- [ ] Check p-value/CI and absolute ΔQ cap
- [ ] If eligible, schedule canary rollout and notify SRE/ops
- [ ] Post-canary: review real-traffic metrics vs eval projection and update spreadsheet with observed delta.

Open questions / TODOs (short list)
- What should the default α be for multi-task models where multiple metrics matter? Proposal: compute a weighted α based on metric importance, but needs product sign-off.
- Integrate unit cost lookup into Optimize service API so spreadsheets can refresh automatically (ticket: OPT-4899).
- Add an automated note in Console when a route-level gate diverges from spreadsheet thresholds (ops-runbook integration).

Next steps (owner -> Evan Brooks)
- Spin up a small pilot with 3 routes: chat-short, summarize-long, embeddings-batch by 2026-03-17.
- Implement a sample DiscountVariantCostModel.xlsx template and push to shared drive. (Asha to own template formatting)
- Create an automation ticket to wire the spreadsheet to the eval runner (OPT-4899).

Appendix: quick reference formulas for spreadsheet copy
- Col H (ΔQ): =F - G
- Col I (ΔC): =D - E
- RelativeQualityLoss: =MAX(0, H / F)
- RelativeCostSaving: =MAX(0, I / D)
- EconomicScore: =RelativeCostSaving / (1 + alpha * RelativeQualityLoss)

End of doc.
